description:
The dataset '/home/ga/Documents/JASP/ExamAnxiety.csv' is already open in JASP. This dataset (Field, 2013) contains exam performance data with columns: 'Code', 'Revise', 'Exam', 'Anxiety', and 'Gender'.

Perform an Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) to test the effect of 'Gender' on 'Exam' performance, controlling for 'Anxiety'.

1. Go to ANOVA > ANCOVA.
2. Set 'Exam' as the Dependent Variable.
3. Set 'Gender' as the Fixed Factor.
4. Set 'Anxiety' as the Covariate.
5. Under 'Display', enable 'Descriptive statistics' and 'Estimates of effect size' (select η² or partial η²).
6. Under 'Marginal Means', move 'Gender' to the right to calculate adjusted means.
7. Under 'Assumption Checks', enable 'Homogeneity of regression slopes' to test the interaction.

Save the JASP analysis file as '/home/ga/Documents/JASP/ExamAnxiety_ANCOVA.jasp'.

Create a text report at '/home/ga/Documents/JASP/ancova_report.txt' containing the following values derived from your analysis:
- F-statistic and p-value for the Anxiety covariate
- F-statistic and p-value for the Gender main effect
- The effect size (η²) for Gender
- The adjusted marginal means for Male and Female
- The p-value for the Homogeneity of Regression Slopes assumption check
- A one-sentence conclusion on whether Gender has a significant effect after controlling for Anxiety.
